tests.title: Unit 4: Books of Second Entry — Ledger – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: A ledger account has debit entries of Rs 45,000 and credit entries of Rs 38,500. The closing balance is:
options: Rs 6,500 debit, brought down on the credit side
Rs 83,500 debit, brought down on the debit side
Rs 6,500 debit, brought down as balance b/d on the debit side
Rs 6,500 credit, brought down as balance b/d on the credit side

questions.question_text: In a ledger, the account of Mr. Rao shows: Dr — balance b/d 12,000, sales 8,000; Cr — returns 1,500, cash 10,000. His closing balance is:
options: Rs 8,500 debit, being the amount he still owes
Rs 20,000 debit, being the total of debits
Rs 11,500 debit, being the total of credits
Rs 8,500 credit, being the amount owed to him

questions.question_text: The ledger account of a creditor shows opening balance Rs 15,000 (Cr), purchases Rs 22,000, payments Rs 30,000 and returns Rs 2,000. The closing balance is:
options: Rs 69,000 credit, representing the total entries
Rs 9,000 credit, representing the amount payable
Rs 5,000 credit, representing the amount payable
Rs 5,000 debit, representing the amount receivable

questions.question_text: While posting, the account to be debited for a credit sale of Rs 9,000 to Mr. Sen is:
options: The cash account in the cash book
The stock account in the general ledger
Mr. Sen's personal account in the debtors ledger
The sales account in the nominal ledger

questions.question_text: The sales account, after posting Rs 5,00,000 sales and Rs 20,000 sales returns, shows:
options: A nil balance since returns are equal to sales
A credit balance of Rs 5,00,000 and returns shown separately
A debit balance of Rs 4,80,000 transferred to trading
A credit balance of Rs 5,20,000 including the returns
questions.explanation: Returns are recorded in a separate account and netted in the trading account.

questions.question_text: Which ledger account is NOT closed at the end of the year by transfer?
Closing balance of an account is written on the side that makes the:
options: Debit side bigger than the credit
Credit side bigger than the debit
Totals of the two sides equal

questions.question_text: The sub-division of the ledger into sales ledger, purchase ledger and general ledger is made to:
options: Eliminate the need for a trial balance
Avoid the use of a journal
Divide work and permit specialised control

questions.question_text: A control account is best described as a:
options: Summary account used to check the accuracy of a subsidiary ledger
Real account kept to record the cash balances of the business
Personal account opened in the name of each debtor of the firm
Nominal account opened to record the expenses of the period

options: The firm has not paid for the goods which it bought on credit
The creditor has allowed a large cash discount to the firm
The firm has made large purchases on credit during the period

questions.question_text: A suspense account is a temporary account opened to:
options: Record the transactions which are not material
Hold the difference when a trial balance does not agree
Record only the proprietor's private transactions
Replace the cash book at the year end

questions.question_text: The trial balance shows the debit total Rs 8,42,000 and the credit total Rs 8,50,000. The suspense account shows:
If an account of capital has a debit balance, it means:
options: The firm has paid its liabilities in full
The firm has earned profit in excess of drawings
The firm has borrowed money from the owner

questions.question_text: If the closing balance of the cash account is carried forward, it is written on the credit side as:
options: Balance c/d, then brought down on the debit side as balance b/d
Balance c/d, then brought down on the credit side
Balance b/d on the debit side only
Balance b/d, then carried down on the credit side as balance c/d

questions.question_text: An error of casting in the ledger means:
options: Posting of a wrong amount from the journal
Posting to the wrong side of an account
Omission of a posting from the journal
Wrong totalling of one side of an account

questions.question_text: Total of the debit side was added as Rs 50,000 instead of Rs 52,000. The trial balance will show a difference of:
options: Rs 2,000, with the debit side short
Rs 2,000, with the credit side short
Rs 4,000, with the debit side short

Cash in hand as per physical verification

options: Brought down to the next period

Dr Sales ledger control; Cr Purchase ledger control

Nil, since the debit side shortfall of Rs 5,000 is cleared
Rs 10,000 on the credit side after the correction
Rs 5,000 on the credit side after the correction

Purchases recorded in the sales book
